name: Perseverance's parachute and backshell

location.name: Jezero crater, around Perseverance's landing site

headline: The biggest parachute ever opened on Mars, with a secret message woven into it
story: On 18 February 2021, Perseverance hit the Martian atmosphere at nearly 20,000 kilometers per hour. Its parachute, 21.5 meters wide and the biggest ever deployed on Mars, opened above Jezero crater. Its orange and white panels hid a binary code: the inner rings spelled "DARE MIGHTY THINGS", the motto of NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory.

About 2.1 kilometers above the ground, the parachute and the cone-shaped backshell it was tied to were let go. The rover dropped away beneath its own sky crane and landed safely. The parachute and backshell fell together and struck the crater floor at about 126 kilometers per hour.

In April 2022, the Ingenuity helicopter flew over them on its 26th flight and photographed them from 8 meters up, at the request of engineers planning to return samples from Mars. The backshell sits upright, its suspension lines streaming across the sand to the parachute. Both still lie where they fell.

facts.label: Parachute
facts.value: 21.5 m wide, the biggest ever deployed on Mars

facts.label: Hidden message
facts.value: "DARE MIGHTY THINGS" in binary, plus JPL's GPS coordinates

images.caption: 18 February 2021: a camera on the backshell looks up at the parachute during descent. The annotations decode the binary message hidden in its stripes.
19 April 2022, from 8 meters up: Ingenuity finds the backshell sitting upright, its suspension lines running to the parachute at upper left.
The debris field from the air: the backshell left of center and the parachute at far right.
